transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

Hi. Well, what finally made me call the employee assistance program is that I’m just barely sleeping right. I'll go to bed and just lie there, replaying work stuff and arguments from home. Then I end up waking up around 3 or 4 in the morning, and... I just start the day feeling like I never really rested at all.
Do you find it hard to stop or control the worrying when it starts?

Um, I wouldn't really say it's hard to control. Like, during the day, if I need to focus on a client or a meeting, I can turn it off just fine. It's not like I'm spiraling or panicking. It's just... when I'm lying in bed and it's quiet, my brain just kind of defaults to chewing on the day's problems. But I don't feel like I've lost control of my thoughts or anything like that.
Lately, have you been feeling down or depressed?

Yeah, I have. Most days, it feels like this heavy, gray mood just follows me around. Like, from the office, to the car, and into the house. Even when nothing specific is going on, I just... I just feel kind of hollow.
Have you had any thoughts that life isn’t worth living, or thoughts of hurting yourself?

I mean... I'm not making a plan to actually hurt myself or anything like that. But, yeah, the thought does come up more than I want to admit. Sometimes I just think... maybe everyone would be better off if I just didn't wake up one morning.
Have you stopped enjoying things you usually like to do?

Yeah, I have. Um, I used to really look forward to playing pickup basketball, or going to bowling nights. I liked going to music festivals, and even just firing up the smoker for friends on the weekend. But lately, I either just end up canceling my plans, or if I do show up, I feel like I'm just going through the motions. I'm just not getting any enjoyment out of it anymore.
Did these mood and sleep problems start after a specific stressful event or change in your life?
Yeah, I think so. This has all been going on for about a year and two months now. That's right around the time the arguments at home started getting a lot worse.
Even on days when things at home are relatively calm, do you still feel depressed?

Yeah, I do. It's like... most days, I feel like this heavy, gray mood just follows me everywhere. It goes with me from the office, to the car, and into the house. So even when things are calm and nothing specific is going wrong, I still just feel kind of hollow.
For at least two weeks at a time, have you felt depressed nearly every day?

Yeah, it's definitely been more than two weeks. Like I was saying, it's pretty much every day. That heavy, gray feeling just stays with me, you know? It doesn't really matter if I'm at work, driving, or at home... it's just this constant hollow feeling that doesn't go away.
Have you noticed a change in your appetite lately?

Yeah, my appetite has been off for a while now... probably for months. I just don't feel like eating much during the day. I'll usually just run on coffee all the way through lunch, and then when I get home, I just kind of pick at dinner with my family. But the weird thing is, even though I'm not really eating much, I've noticed my belt is sitting a notch tighter than it used to.
Have you been feeling worthless or like you’ve let other people down?

Yeah, I do. I... I keep replaying things in my head. Like every late night I stayed at work, every time I went to a tailgate instead of being home, every dumb purchase I've made. I just end up thinking that my wife and kids got stuck with a selfish guy, and that I just keep letting them down.
If the problems at home were resolved, do you think you’d still feel this depressed?

I don't know... I mean, fixing things at home would probably help some, but... honestly, I think I'd still feel this way. It's like this feeling is just stuck to me, regardless of what's actually happening around me.
Have you been moving or speaking noticeably slower than usual lately?

Yeah, I have. I mean, people at work probably wouldn’t say I’m falling apart or anything, but I can definitely tell I move slower. I'll just sit there staring at my laptop a lot longer than I used to. And sometimes it just... takes me a beat too long to answer my reps when they ask me something simple.
Have you been feeling unusually tired or low on energy lately?
No, not really. I mean... I get regular tired after a long day at work, but nothing unusual. My physical energy is mostly fine, so I wouldn't say I feel wiped out or anything like that.
Have you been having trouble concentrating?

Yeah, I have. I used to be able to knock out sales forecasts and client decks pretty quickly, but now... I don't know, I'll read the same slide five times. I just end up second-guessing every number, and I still can’t decide what to say. It's been really frustrating trying to get things done.
Before these past year of mood symptoms started, were you already having trouble sleeping?

No, not really. Before this past year, my sleep was fine. I mean, maybe I'd have an occasional restless night if we had a big quarter closing or something, but... no, I didn't have any real trouble sleeping back then.
Have you gained weight lately?

Yeah, I have. I noticed recently that my belt is sitting a notch tighter than it used to. It's kind of weird, though, because my appetite has actually been off for months. I mean, I'll usually just run on coffee through lunch, and then... I mostly just pick at dinner with my family. But somehow, yeah, I've still put on a little weight.
Have these symptoms made it hard for you to function at work or at home?

Yeah, it has. I mean, I’m still showing up to work every day, but... my team has definitely had to cover some gaps for me. When my forecasts and client prep slip like I was talking about, they end up having to pick up the slack. And then at home... I don't know, I’m just less present with my wife and kids than I used to be. I'm physically there, but I'm not really engaging with them the way I should be.
